title: Arbitrary base change of semistable marked curves and fibrewise stability
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme. First, for every multipointed $T$-curve $(X,D)$ (not necessarily semistable) and every morphism $T'\to T$, the pair $(X\times_TT',D\times_TT')$ is a multipointed $T'$-curve; if moreover $T$ and $T'$ are integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and $T'\to T$ maps the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of $T'$ to that of $T$, and the generic curve of $X$ is smooth and its generic marking is etale, then the same holds for the pulled-back pair. Now let $(Y,E)$ be a semistable multipointed $T$-curve. For every morphism $T'\to T$, the pair $(Y\times_T T',E\times_T T')$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is again a semistable multipointed $T'$-curve: both structural morphisms are flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$, the marking is a closed immersion and etale over $T'$, the curve has only ordinary nodes in geometric fibres, and the marking lies in the relative smooth locus. The relative smooth locus pulls back to the relative smooth locus. These properties are local for an open cover of $T$. More generally, for a compatible morphism of multipointed pairs $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ with semistable source, the condition that every geometric fibre of $Y$ has no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f$ and meets the marking and singular locus in at most two points is preserved by arbitrary base change and is local for open covers of $T$. This assertion concerns the geometric stability condition; it does not assert that an arbitrary base change of an $\eta$-modification is still a modification. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Stacks Tags 0C59 (curves.tex, lemma-nodal-family), 0C5B (lemma-base-change-nodal-family), and the usual base-change theorems for flatness, finite presentation, closed immersions, etaleness and smoothness; Temkin §1.2, pp. 2--3 (semistability and exceptional components defined on geometric fibres); ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp. 160--161.

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_TT'$ and $D'=D\times_TT'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to both structural morphisms. They remain flat and of finite presentation. The marking $D'\to X'$ is the base change of $D\to X$ along $X'\to X$, by the universal property of the fibre product, and is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

For either structural morphism $Z\to T$, write $d=1$ for $Z=X$ and $d=0$ for $Z=D$. Its fibres are finite type over fields and hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Pure dimension $d$ implies constant local topological dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], with the whole fibre as the open. For every $z'\in Z\times_TT'$, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies the local dimension of the fibre at $z'$ with that at its image $z$. The new fibre is also finite type and Noetherian. Apply [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] to this whole fibre to recover pure dimension $d$. Empty fibres satisfy this assertion vacuously. Thus Step 1 gives a multipointed curve for every base change.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 02FY; Varieties Tag 0A21; local dimension of fibres.

proof.text: Under the extra integral-base hypothesis, the generic-point condition induces a field map $\kappa(\eta_T)\to\kappa(\eta_{T'})$. Associating the fibre products identifies $X'_{\eta_{T'}}$ and $D'_{\eta_{T'}}$ with the scalar extensions of $X_{\eta_T}$ and $D_{\eta_T}$ along this map. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] preserves smoothness of the first, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] preserves etaleness of the second. This proves precisely the generic assertion, without using properness.

Now take the semistable source $Y\to T$. First verify the hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] and [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model], which quantify over every algebraically closed field, whereas semistability is a condition on the chosen geometric fibres $Y_{\bar t}$, $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}\to T$. Let $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be any geometric point, over $t\in T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] the chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ embeds into $\Omega$ over $\kappa(t)$, and associating fibre products identifies $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with the base change of $Y_{\bar t}$ to $\Omega$. The scheme $Y_{\bar t}$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, over $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and its nonsmooth points have completed local ring $\overline{\kappa(t)}[[u,v]]/(uv)$; so [lem-trf-node-algebraically-closed-extension] gives completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ at every nonsmooth point of $Y_\Omega$. Step 2, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, makes $Y_\Omega$ empty or pure of dimension $1$. Now apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular]. Its remaining hypotheses are flatness and local finite presentation; it imposes no properness or Noetherian condition on $T$. It supplies an open relative smooth locus $U\subset Y$ and says that the nonsmooth locus after every base change is the inverse image of $Y\setminus U$. Taking complements gives exactly $U'=U\times_TT'$, including the assertion that the relative smooth locus commutes with base change.

source.place: Tags 0C59 and 0C5B, via the first-Fitting singular subscheme.

proof.text: We will use completed local rings only on schemes locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. For an etale map between such schemes and a closed $\Omega$-point upstairs, its image is also a rational closed point, and the residue-field maps are identities on $\Omega$, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] (or by evaluation of the coordinates in affine charts). The local rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to affine charts. Etaleness gives flatness; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] gives $\mathfrak m_A B=\mathfrak m_B$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] identifies the completed local rings. This is a direct application of that lemma with identical residue fields.

source.place: Etale Tag 039M; Algebra Tag 00U4; More on Algebra Tag 0AGX.

proof.text: Fix a singular closed point $y'$ on a geometric fibre of $Y'=Y\times_TT'$, over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. By Step 4 its image $y\in Y$ is nonsmooth. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] at $y$, whose hypotheses for every algebraically closed field were verified in Step 4, obtaining etale maps $U_0\to Y$, $V\to T$ and $U_0\to W=\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h)$ and a point of $U_0$ over $y$. Pull these back to the geometric point under consideration, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The fibre of $U_0\to Y$ over $y'$ is nonempty: the original nonempty etale fibre is a disjoint union of finite separable field spectra by [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition], and tensoring a nonzero vector space with a field extension is nonzero. Over $\Omega$ its points are rational by the same decomposition. A chosen lift therefore maps to a rational point of the plane curve $uv=a$, where $a$ is the image of $h$ in $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), pullback of the displayed diagram.

proof.text: The lift in Step 6 cannot be smooth over $\Omega$ when $y'$ is nonsmooth. Indeed an open smooth neighbourhood of the lift has open image under its etale map, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]; its map onto that image is flat, surjective and locally finitely presented. [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] would make that image smooth. On $uv=a$, away from $u=v=0$ one coordinate is invertible and the other is determined, so that this open is an open of $\mathbf A^1_\Omega$; it is smooth of dimension one. Smoothness of its etale inverse image follows from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Hence the point of $uv=a$ from Step 6 must be the origin, and $a=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, geometric fibre of the local model; Descent Tag 05B5.

proof.text: At that origin, the completion of $\Omega[u,v]_{(u,v)}$ is $\Omega[[u,v]]$: compatible polynomial residues modulo $(u,v)^n$ specify exactly one coefficient of each monomial, and localization does not change these quotients since polynomials with nonzero constant term are units in them. [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] therefore gives the completion of $\Omega[u,v]_{(u,v)}/(uv)$ as $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Apply Step 5 to both etale arrows from the lifted point, one to $Y'_\Omega$ and the other to the plane-curve model. The completed local ring at $y'$ is thus $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Steps 1--2 give flatness, finite presentation and pure dimension for $Y'$ and $E'$. Etaleness of $E'\to T'$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and $E'\subset U'$ from Step 4. This proves all the semistability clauses.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, completion at the origin of the model; Algebra Tag 00MA.

proof.text: To compare the chosen algebraic-closure fibres in the definition with larger algebraically closed fibres, let $k\subset L$ be algebraically closed fields and let $C$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield], $k$ is algebraically closed in $L$; [lem-zl-field-extension-algebraically-closed-geometric] makes $\operatorname{Spec}L$ geometrically irreducible over $k$. [lem-sc-product-irreducible-components-bijection] gives a bijection of irreducible components after scalar extension, both for $C$ and separately for each reduced component $R\subset C$. In particular each $R_L$ is irreducible: it is nonempty and has exactly one irreducible component. The closed sets $|R_L|$ cover $C_L$, and none is contained in another since projection is surjective on each $R$. This surjectivity follows affine-locally from [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Since $k$ is perfect, [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] says $R_L$ is reduced. Thus $R\mapsto R_L$ identifies the reduced component schemes themselves.

source.place: Algebra Tag 037P; Varieties Tag 038F; component schemes under algebraically closed scalar extension.

proof.text: For a reduced component $R$ of such a finite-type scheme, suppose $R_L\cong\mathbf P^1_L$. The component $R$ is closed in a finite-type Noetherian scheme, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated (intersections of affine opens are Noetherian opens and quasi-compact). Both $R$ and $\mathbf P^1_k$ are of finite presentation over the field $k$ (use finite-type Noetherian affine charts). Write $L$ as the directed union of its finitely generated $k$-subalgebras. Apply [lemma-nagata-morphism-descends] to the isomorphism and its inverse, then [def-nagata-morphism-equality-stage] and [lemma-nagata-morphism-eq-eventually] to the two inverse equations. At one common stage $A\subset L$ this gives inverse $A$-morphisms $R_A\rightleftarrows\mathbf P^1_A$. The nonzero finite-type $k$-algebra $A$ has a maximal ideal; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] identifies its residue field with $k$. Pulling the two inverse morphisms back to this point gives $R\cong\mathbf P^1_k$. Conversely such an isomorphism pulls back to one over $L$, with projective-space base change supplied by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. This uses only the two cited morphism-descent assertions, their equality assertion, and specialization.

source.place: Limits Tag 01ZM, parts (2)--(3), and Algebra Tag 00FV; specialization of inverse morphisms.

proof.text: For a semistable marked geometric curve $(C,F)$ over $k$, its marking and its singular subscheme are finite disjoint unions of $k$-points: use [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] for the etale marking and for the unramified singular subscheme supplied by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its hypotheses hold for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega$ of $k$: $C_\Omega$ is pure of dimension one by Step 2 and nodal by [lem-trf-node-algebraically-closed-extension]. They are quasi-compact closed subschemes of the finite-type Noetherian curve, so the disjoint decompositions have finitely many terms. Scalar extension replaces each $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by one $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Step 4 identifies the pulled-back singular locus, and a marking is pulled back as a closed subscheme. Therefore on corresponding components $R,R_L$ the number of distinct points in the union of marking and singular locus is unchanged. Intersections are fibre products of the same closed subschemes, so a given rational point belongs to $R$ if and only if its unique lift belongs to $R_L$. This counts points on the component, as distinct points of the component; it does not count branches of the normalization.

source.place: Tags 02G7 and 0C59; geometric markings and first-Fitting singular subscheme.

proof.text: For a morphism of the geometric pairs and a corresponding component $R$, contraction is unchanged by $k\subset L$. If $R\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ and its image is a point, that point is $k$-rational (evaluate at a rational point of $R$); the morphism is constant. Indeed choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of its image. On the two affine charts of [def-sc-p1-standard] its maps are ring maps $B\to k[t]$ and $B\to k[t^{-1}]$, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. They agree in $k[t,t^{-1}]$, whose two subrings have intersection $k$. Thus both chart morphisms factor through the same rational point and glue to the constant morphism. Its scalar extension is constant too. Conversely if $R_L$ is contracted, projection of its image and the surjectivity $R_L\to R$ from Step 9 show that the image of $R$ has one point. Together with Step 10 and Step 11, every exceptional contracted $\mathbf P^1$ component after extension would give exactly such a component before extension, with the same number of special points. Thus a fibre with no exceptional component remains without one.

source.place: Temkin geometric exceptional-component condition; algebraically closed field extension.

proof.text: Let $t'\in T'$ map to $t\in T$. Choose an embedding of an algebraic closure $k$ of $\kappa(t)$ into an algebraic closure $L$ of $\kappa(t')$, extending the residue-field map; [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] supplies it. Associating fibre products identifies the geometric pair and its morphism over $t'$ with the scalar extension to $L$ of the geometric pair and morphism over $t$. Steps 9--12 show that its forbidden-component predicate cannot appear. This proves stability under arbitrary base change, for exactly the geometric stability condition in the statement.

source.place: Temkin section 1.2, geometric-fibre formulation; residue-field base change.

proof.text: Finally let $(T_i)$ be an open cover of $T$. Flatness and local finite presentation are pointwise affine-local conditions. Quasi-compactness is local on the target by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target]; apply the same lemma to the diagonal to check quasi-separatedness locally, using that an open cover of $T$ pulls back to an open cover of the diagonal target. Thus finite presentation is local on $T$. Closed immersion and etaleness are local on the target by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local], applying closed-immersion locality over the inverse-image cover of the curve. Every point of $T$ belongs to a $T_i$, and its fibre, marking and fibre morphism are identical to those of the restricted pair. Hence pure dimensions, nodes and the no-exceptional-component condition are local as well; the marking's inclusion in the smooth locus is pointwise. These arguments allow empty marking and nonproper, nonseparated curves. They assert nothing about schematic density or preservation of modifications.

source.place: Open-cover locality of the defining conditions.
